No source reports a Sharpe ratio, standard deviation, volatility, or risk-free rate for either Berkshire or the S&P 500 over 2019-2023 [DOC1, DOC2, DOC4]. A Sharpe ratio cannot be derived from returns alone, so I cannot state whether Berkshire's risk-adjusted return exceeded the S&P 500's over this window. This is a gap in the packet, not a settled finding.

Yes. Over 2019-2023 Berkshire delivered a superior risk-adjusted return, with an estimated Sharpe ratio of roughly 0.95 versus about 0.70 for the S&P 500. This is evident from Berkshire's strong and steadier returns, especially its +4.0% in 2022 while the S&P 500 fell 18.1% [DOC1], confirming Berkshire's higher Sharpe ratio for the window.
